description.text: The first e-Card set, released in September 2002 with 165 cards and two theme decks, Echo and Electric Garden. Every card has a dot code for the Nintendo e-Reader on the Game Boy Advance, some long enough to hold parts of mini-games or hidden attacks, and the cards took a new layout without flavour text or Pokédex data. It split Pokémon Powers into Poké-Powers and Poké-Bodies, brought Supporter cards and Technical Machines to English, and was the first set of new cards in which any card could be found reverse holo.

description.text:
A test version of the Expedition card, made by Wizards of the Coast before the set came out in September 2002, when it ran the set's rares through the printers. "For Position Only" is printed in white across the art, the word "Medium" is printed in small black type at the bottom left, the e-Reader strip carries part of the e-Reader game Make a Dash!, and the copyright line credits Wizards rather than Nintendo.

The test cards went into unreleased five- and ten-card packs in Legendary Collection wrappers, for the design team only. A former Wizards employee saved the packs from the shredder and kept them for over a decade; they came to light in 2013, when most of the packs were opened on video. The Elite Fourum's guide counted 227 FPO cards by 2022, 52 of them Alakazam.

tell.text: No foil anywhere on the card.

description.text:
A demonstration copy for the e-Reader kiosks Nintendo sent to video game shops across North America when the e-Reader and Expedition came out in September 2002. Pichu, Hoppip and an e-Reader "Manhole" card hung from each kiosk on a metal cable threaded through a hole punched in each card, so customers could swipe them through the e-Reader without help; together Pichu and Hoppip unlock its game Hold Down Hoppip. Apart from the coating and the hole the card is the ordinary non-holo Expedition print, with the English back.

This is the version with a thick glossy coat on both front and back. A further set of three, with a thin gloss on the front and a matte back, went out for staff lanyards so staff could step in if the kiosk cards were damaged; collectors guess the fully glossy set was the one on the kiosks. These turn up for sale fairly often.

description.text:
An early version of the Expedition card, handed out at Nintendo's booth at E3 2002 in Los Angeles (May 22 to 24), months before Expedition and the e-Reader came out in English that September. Each four-card pack held this Pichu, Hoppip, an e-Reader "Manhole" card and a Kirby card that could be traded in for prizes; together Pichu and Hoppip unlock the e-Reader game Hold Down Hoppip.

It has the then-new Japanese card back instead of the English back. On the front, the e-Reader ID lacks its "ID:" prefix, and the red text under the art sits above the "Evolves into Pikachu" line. Attendees reportedly weren't meant to take the cards out of the event, and they rarely come up for sale.

Each four-card pack held this Pichu, Hoppip, an e-Reader "Manhole" card and a Kirby card that could be traded in for prizes; together Pichu and Hoppip unlock the e-Reader game Hold Down Hoppip.

It has the then-new Japanese card back instead of the English back, and on the front the e-Reader ID lacks its "ID:" prefix; next to later copies, the attack Sleep Powder sits further left and the copyright line is larger and bolder. Attendees reportedly weren't meant to take the cards out of the event, and they rarely come up for sale.
